target: Il a pris sa retraite l'année dernière.
english: He retired last year.
tip: To retire is 'prendre sa retraite' – literally take one's retirement. 'Il a pris sa retraite' = he retired.

target: Elle a vu quelque chose de bizarre.
english: She saw something strange.
tip: Slip 'de' before the adjective: 'quelque chose de bizarre', literally something OF strange. Same with quelqu'un de gentil, rien de neuf.

target: Nous avons fait connaissance à une soirée.
english: We met at a party.
tip: 'Faire connaissance' – literally make acquaintance – is how you say you first met someone. 'Nous avons fait connaissance' = we met.

target: Elles ont été très gentilles avec nous.
english: They were very kind to us.
tip: You're kind 'avec' someone, not 'to' them: 'gentilles avec nous' = kind to us. French uses with where English uses to.

target: Il a été surpris de me voir.
english: He was surprised to see me.
tip: The object pronoun comes before the verb: 'me voir' = to see me, literally 'me to-see'. Little words like me sit in front, not after.

target: Elle essayait de nouveaux plats chaque semaine.
english: She used to try new dishes every week.
tip: Before a plural adjective, 'des' shrinks to 'de': 'de nouveaux plats', not des nouveaux plats. Compare de beaux jardins.

target: Elle chantait sous la douche chaque matin.
english: She sang in the shower every morning.
tip: Repeated actions in the past use imparfait. Chaque matin signals a habit.

target: Je pensais que c'était une bonne idée.
english: I thought it was a good idea.
tip: Mental states in the past use imparfait: je pensais, je croyais, je savais.

target: Nous attendions le bus sous la pluie.
english: We were waiting for the bus in the rain.
tip: 'Attendre' already means wait FOR – no extra word needed: 'attendions le bus' = waited for the bus. Adding 'pour' would be wrong.

target: Nous avons vu un beau coucher de soleil.
english: We saw a beautiful sunset.
tip: A sunset is a 'coucher de soleil' – literally the sun's lying-down. Sunrise flips it: lever de soleil, the sun getting up.

target: Nous avons écrit un rapport de dix pages.
english: We wrote a ten-page report.
tip: 'Ten-page' becomes 'de dix pages' after the noun: 'un rapport de dix pages'. French hangs the measurement off the noun with de.

target: Tu as eu des nouvelles de Pierre ?
english: Did you hear from Pierre?
tip: To hear from someone is 'avoir des nouvelles de' – literally have news of. 'Des nouvelles de Pierre' = word from Pierre.

target: Il a fait ses devoirs avant de sortir.
english: He did his homework before going out.
tip: Before doing something, use 'avant de' + the plain verb: 'avant de sortir' = before going out, literally before to-go-out.

target: Il a dit la meme chose que moi.
english: He said the same thing as me.
tip: 'The same as' is 'la même... que': 'la même chose que moi' = the same thing as me. And it's moi, the stressed form, never je.

target: Il a pris un rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
english: He made an appointment at the dentist.
tip: 'Chez' means at someone's place or office: 'chez le dentiste' = at the dentist's. Use chez with people, not à.

target: Tu as mis la lettre dans l'enveloppe ?
english: Did you put the letter in the envelope?
tip: 'Mettre' also means 'to take (time)': 'J'ai mis deux heures' = It took me two hours. Very common usage.

target: J'ai fait un rêve vraiment bizarre cette nuit.
english: I had a really bizarre dream last night.
tip: You don't 'have' a dream in French, you make one: 'j'ai fait un rêve' = I had a dream. It's faire, not avoir, with rêve.

target: Il y avait un beau parc près de chez nous.
english: There was a beautiful park near our house.
tip: Il y avait (there was or there were) uses imparfait to describe past situations.

target: Nous apprenions l'espagnol au collège.
english: We were learning Spanish in middle school.
tip: 'Collège' is middle school, not college – a classic false friend. 'Au collège' means roughly ages 11 to 15. University is la fac.

target: Il conduisait un vieux camion bleu.
english: He drove an old blue truck.
tip: Colours land after the noun, but age words go before: 'un vieux camion bleu' = an old blue truck. Vieux leads, bleu trails.

target: J'ai eu envie de partir en voyagé.
english: I felt like taking a trip.
tip: 'Avoir envie de' means to feel like, not to envy: 'j'ai eu envie de partir' = I felt like leaving. French 'has' the urge.

target: Je lisais quand le téléphone a sonné.
english: I was reading when the phone rang.
tip: Imparfait for the ongoing action (lisais), passé composé for the interruption (a sonné).

target: Nous avions l'habitude de dîner à vingt heures.
english: We used to have dinner at eight PM.
tip: 'Avoir l'habitude de' = to be used to, literally 'to have the habit of': 'nous avions l'habitude de dîner' = we usually had dinner.

target: Je marchais dans la rue quand j'ai vu un vieil ami.
english: I was walking down the street when I saw an old friend.
tip: Imparfait sets the scene (marchais), passé composé introduces a new event (ai vu).

target: Nous adorions les vacances d'été.
english: We loved summer vacation.
tip: To love something in general, French adds 'les': 'adorions les vacances' = loved vacations. English drops the article here; French never does.

target: Elle me l'a dit hier.
english: She told me yesterday.
tip: Double pronouns: me + le becomes me l'. Order: me/te/se/nous/vous + le/la/les.

target: Nous le connaissons depuis l'enfance.
english: We've known him since childhood.
tip: With 'depuis', French stays in the present for something still true: 'nous le connaissons depuis l'enfance' = we've known him since childhood.

target: Nous mangions ensemble tous les dimanches.
english: We used to eat together every Sunday.
tip: 'Tous les dimanches' (every Sunday) is a clear habit marker → imparfait is the right tense.

target: Ils jouaient aux cartes tous les vendredis.
english: They used to play cards every Friday.
tip: 'Jouer à' is for games and sports: 'jouaient aux cartes' = played cards (à + les = aux). Instruments switch to 'jouer de'.

target: Tu te souvenais de cette chanson ?
english: Did you used to remember this song?
tip: 'Se souvenir' needs both a reflexive pronoun and 'de': 'te souvenais de cette chanson' = remembered this song. The 'de' is not optional.
